title: Indexes [Expression-based]
description:
## Expression-based Indexes
Normal indexes work on a column as-is. But what if you always search with a function like `LOWER()` or `LENGTH()`?
```sql
-- This query can't use a normal index on name
SELECT * FROM users WHERE LOWER(name) = 'steve';
```
An expression-based index indexes the RESULT of an expression:
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_lower_name ON users(LOWER(name));
```
Now `WHERE LOWER(name) = 'steve'` is fast because the index stores the lowercased values.

Common uses:
- `LOWER(column)` - case-insensitive searches
- `LENGTH(column)` - searching by string length
- `SUBSTR(column, 1, 3)` - searching by prefix

---
## Assignment:
BWS searches tickets by lowercase title all the time. Create an expression-based index called `idx_lower_title` on `LOWER(title)` of the tickets table.
